rachel: Heads-up — our edge sample's TS inference regressed after switching to a single esbuild bundle. Generic calls like `client.parse<MyType>()` end up inferred as `any` in consuming apps. Runtime is fine. Anyone seen this pattern?

marco: Yup. Usually caused by an overload fallback or by differing module resolution between how we build the runtime bundle and how tsc resolves types. Can you paste the callsite + the declaration that looks wrong?

ivy: Also check if sample CI uses `skipLibCheck`. That hides a lot of cross-package mismatches.

rachel: callsite:

```ts
const res = await client.parse<{ user: { id: string } }>({ model: 'edge-mini', input: 'x' });
// expecting res.user.id: string, but TS says any after CI types check
```

and declaration in `node_modules/@redwood/inference/index.d.ts`:

```ts
parse<T>(opts: ParseOptions & { format: 'json' }): Promise<T>
parse(opts: ParseOptions): Promise<any>
```

marco: There's the smoking gun: the fallback returns `Promise<any>`. When the compiler can't conclusively pick the first overload (common across module boundaries or when types are flattened), it falls back to the wider signature and you lose inference.

ivy: Two practical fixes: 1) make the fallback generic `parse<T = any>(opts: ParseOptions): Promise<T>` to preserve inference, or 2) return `Promise<unknown>` and provide a small explicit cast helper e.g. `asParsed<T>(v: unknown): T`. I prefer `unknown` for public surface area.

rachel: Love the `unknown` approach from a correctness standpoint, but it will surface new type errors in user code. We need to be careful about breaking customers.

marco: We should also verify package publishing: are we shipping both ESM and CJS with matching `types`? Some bundlers prefer different entrypoints and that can cause the compiler to pick a different `.d.ts` file when consumers use `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` vs `node16`/`nodenext`.

rachel: Our package.json points `types` to `dist/index.d.ts`. We only publish that single d.ts, but our build pipeline creates both `dist/esm/index.js` and `dist/cjs/index.js`. The rollup step sometimes emits flattened declaration files (rollup-plugin-dts) that change overload shapes.

ivy: Exactly. Flattening can lose overload order or inline union types leading to weaker inference. Add a dts snapshot test that asserts the expected overload strings exist in `dist/index.d.ts` before publishing.

ci-bot: CI types job failed in samples/edge-ts: `samples/edge-ts/src/main.ts:17 Type 'any' is not assignable to type '{ user: { id: string } }'`. See job: https://ci.internal/1122

marco: For immediate relief, rachel: can you try changing the fallback to `Promise<T = any>` and run the samples matrix? That preserves inference without forcing users to change code. Then we can follow up with a safer `unknown` migration and a changelog.

rachel: Will do. Also noticed `skipLibCheck: true` in the sample tsconfig to speed CI. I'm going to turn that off for the edge-ts job so these mismatches fail fast.

ivy: Also ensure sample tsconfigs match the target runtime: for esbuild-based edge bundles use `module: "ESNext"` and `moduleResolution: "bundler"`. For node targets use `module: "Node16"` / `moduleResolution: "nodenext"`. Mismatched resolution picks different `.d.ts` variants in some edge cases.

marco: Don't forget `esModuleInterop` and `allowSyntheticDefaultImports` — those flip import shapes and can indirectly influence which typescript resolution path is used by tsc. Keep them documented in samples README.

rachel: Plan: 1) quick patch: fallback -> `Promise<T = any>` so existing callers keep inference, 2) add tsd tests asserting `parse<MyType>` infers `MyType`, 3) add dts snapshot test to CI, 4) update edge sample tsconfig to `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` and remove `skipLibCheck` in CI, 5) open an RFC to migrate fallback -> `unknown` in the next major with migration note.

ivy: +1. Also add a tiny doc snippet in `samples/README.md` that maps runtime -> recommended tsconfig. Saves future confusion.

marco: When you change public types, include a changelog entry and call out the rational in the release notes. Unknown vs any is a behavioral change for consumers.

rachel: I'll open a PR with the fallback tweak + tests and ping y'all. If CI still complains I'll attach the failing artifact.

docs-bot: created docs suggestion: "samples: recommended tsconfig per runtime (edge vs node)" assigned to rachel.

ci-bot: rerun: types job passed after temporary pin to previous SDK types (jobs/1122).

rachel: Thanks everyone — will avoid changing public typings until we have tests and docs ready. :thumbsup:
